title: Blackbox Tool Definitions
description: Canonical tool contract for Blackbox. Every IDE implementation exposes these tools with these names, descriptions, input schemas and annotations; the VS Code extension serves this file over MCP and generates its chat tools from it.

tools.name: ide_list_windows
tools.description: List the editor windows (VS Code, Cursor, and other VS Code-based editors) that this session can control. For each: its editor and version, folders, whether this session uses it (selected), whether this session was started from it (launchedFrom), whether it runs an outdated extension, its breakpoint count, and its debugger state (running, or stopped at file:line). Call it when a call fails because the window is ambiguous or missing, or before debugging when several windows are open; then pick one with ide_select_window.

tools.name: ide_select_window
tools.description: Choose which editor window this session controls, for all following calls. The choice lasts for this session and survives a window reload; if that window closes, calls fail instead of switching to another. Omit window to go back to automatic selection (by working directory, then by the window this session was started from).

window.description: Window id, absolute folder path, or folder name from ide_list_windows (e.g. "wpcore.wpx"). Omit to clear the selection

app.description: Editor name, or part of it (e.g. "Cursor", "Visual Studio Code"), when the same folder is open in several editors

tools.name: debug_set_breakpoint
tools.description: Add source breakpoints: pause when execution reaches a line. Pass one breakpoint as file + line, or several as breakpoints. Supports a condition, a hit count, and logpoints (log a message instead of pausing). Setting it again on the same line adds another breakpoint; check debug_list_breakpoints first. Breakpoints apply to the current and future debug sessions. Returns one "ok:" or "skip:" line per breakpoint, plus a note if the debug adapter can't do hit counts.

file.description: Absolute path of the source file, as it exists in the editor's workspace

condition.description: Pause only when this expression is true, in the debugged language's syntax (e.g. "$count > 5")

hitCondition.description: Pause only on a given hit count: "5" (the 5th hit), ">= 10", "% 3" (every 3rd). Adapter syntax may vary

logMessage.description: Log this message instead of pausing (a logpoint); {expression} parts are evaluated, e.g. "total={$total}". Read it with debug_get_output

file.description: Absolute path of the source file, as it exists in the editor's workspace

condition.description: Pause only when this expression is true, in the debugged language's syntax (e.g. "$count > 5")

hitCondition.description: Pause only on a given hit count: "5" (the 5th hit), ">= 10", "% 3" (every 3rd). Adapter syntax may vary

logMessage.description: Log this message instead of pausing (a logpoint); {expression} parts are evaluated, e.g. "total={$total}". Read it with debug_get_output

breakpoints.description: Several breakpoints at once, instead of file + line

tools.name: debug_set_function_breakpoint
tools.description: Pause when a function is called, by name, without knowing its file and line (e.g. "wp_update_plugins", "MyClass::save", "handleRequest"). Supports a condition, hit count and log message. Not every debug adapter supports function breakpoints (PHP/Xdebug does; the result notes when the active adapter doesn't).

name.description: Function or method name, in the language's notation

condition.description: Pause only when this expression is true, in the debugged language's syntax (e.g. "$count > 5")

hitCondition.description: Pause only on a given hit count: "5" (the 5th hit), ">= 10", "% 3" (every 3rd). Adapter syntax may vary

logMessage.description: Log this message instead of pausing (a logpoint); {expression} parts are evaluated, e.g. "total={$total}". Read it with debug_get_output

tools.name: debug_remove_breakpoint
tools.description: Remove source breakpoints by file and line, and function breakpoints by name. Pass file + line for one, breakpoints for several, and/or functions. Returns one "ok:" or "skip:" line per item. To keep a breakpoint for later, disable it with debug_toggle_breakpoints instead.

file.description: Absolute path of the source file, as it exists in the editor's workspace
Absolute path of the source file, as it exists in the editor's workspace

functions.description: Names of function breakpoints to remove

tools.name: debug_remove_all_breakpoints
tools.description: Remove every breakpoint in the window: source, function and any others, including ones the user set. Consider debug_toggle_breakpoints to disable them instead.

tools.name: debug_list_breakpoints
tools.description: List every breakpoint in the window: source breakpoints (file, line) and function breakpoints (name), with enabled state, condition, hit condition and log message.

tools.name: debug_toggle_breakpoints
tools.description: Enable or disable breakpoints without removing them, keeping their conditions. Pass breakpoints (file + line) and/or functions (names); with neither, applies to every breakpoint. Returns how many changed.

enabled.description: true to enable, false to disable

file.description: Absolute path of the source file, as it exists in the editor's workspace

tools.name: debug_get_launch_configs
tools.description: List the debug launch configurations defined for the workspace (launch.json or the workspace file), per folder, with all their settings (type, request, port, path mappings, adapter options). Call it before debug_start and pass a configuration's name as configName.

tools.name: debug_start
tools.description: Start a debug session. Preferred: pass configName, the name of a launch configuration from debug_get_launch_configs, so all its settings are used as-is. Otherwise pass type and request plus any adapter settings (port, program, pathMappings, and any other launch configuration property). For request-triggered debuggers such as PHP Xdebug, the session only listens: trigger the code afterwards (e.g. an HTTP request with ?XDEBUG_TRIGGER=1, adding a unique query parameter if pages may be cached), then call debug_wait_for_stop.

configName.description: Name of a launch configuration or compound from debug_get_launch_configs

folder.description: Absolute workspace folder path whose configuration to use, when several folders define the same name

type.description: Debug adapter type when not using configName: php, node, python, go, cppdbg, java, ...

request.description: "launch" (start a program, or listen for PHP Xdebug) or "attach" (connect to a running one), when not using configName

port.description: Port the adapter listens on or connects to (e.g. 9003 for Xdebug)

program.description: Absolute path of the program to launch

pathMappings.description: Map of server/remote paths to local paths, e.g. {"/var/www/html": "/Users/me/site"}

tools.name: debug_stop
tools.description: Stop the active debug session, including any child sessions it started; for listeners such as PHP Xdebug this frees the port. Call debug_wait_for_stop afterwards to confirm it reports "terminated".

tools.name: debug_restart
tools.description: Restart the active debug session with the same configuration. If the debug adapter can't restart, the session is stopped instead and the result says so; start it again with debug_start.

tools.name: debug_continue
tools.description: Resume execution of a paused thread (the play button). Does not wait: call debug_wait_for_stop to wait for the next pause. For PHP, other paused requests (threads) stay paused.

threadId.description: Thread id from debug_list_threads (default: the paused thread, else the focused one)

tools.name: debug_pause
tools.description: Pause a running thread (the pause button) and report where it stopped: file, line, function and top frames.

threadId.description: Thread id from debug_list_threads (default: the paused thread, else the focused one)

tools.name: debug_step_over
tools.description: Run the current line, stepping over function calls, and report the new location (file, line, function, top frames). Returns state "running" if it has not paused within 10 seconds (e.g. the line blocks); then call debug_wait_for_stop.

threadId.description: Thread id from debug_list_threads (default: the paused thread, else the focused one)

tools.name: debug_step_into
tools.description: Step into the function called on the current line (or to the next line if there is no call) and report the new location.

threadId.description: Thread id from debug_list_threads (default: the paused thread, else the focused one)

tools.name: debug_step_out
tools.description: Run until the current function returns and report the new location in the caller. Stepping out of the outermost frame runs the program on until its next pause or its end.

threadId.description: Thread id from debug_list_threads (default: the paused thread, else the focused one)

tools.name: debug_run_to_line
tools.description: Continue until a given line is reached ("run to cursor"), using a temporary breakpoint that is always removed afterwards. Reports where it paused; reachedTarget is false if something else paused it first (another breakpoint, an exception) or state is "running" if the line wasn't reached before the timeout.

file.description: Absolute path of the source file, as it exists in the editor's workspace

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait in milliseconds (default 30000, max 300000)

threadId.description: Thread id from debug_list_threads (default: the paused thread, else the focused one)

tools.name: debug_wait_for_stop
tools.description: Wait until the debugger pauses (breakpoint, exception, step, pause) and report the reason, session, thread, file, line, function and top frames. Returns at once if it is already paused, unless next is true. Use after debug_start or debug_continue, or after triggering the code. Returns state "running" on timeout, which is not an error: call it again to keep waiting. Returns state "terminated" when no debug session is left.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait in milliseconds (default 30000, max 300000)

next.description: Wait for a new pause even if already paused, e.g. another PHP request (thread) hitting a breakpoint while one is paused

tools.name: debug_list_threads
tools.description: List the threads of the active debug session, marking the paused ones. For PHP/Xdebug each concurrent HTTP request is its own thread; pass a thread id as threadId to other tools to act on that request.

tools.name: debug_get_stack_trace
tools.description: Get the call stack of a paused thread: frame id, function, file and line for each frame, innermost first. Pass a frame id as frameId to debug_get_variables, debug_evaluate, debug_inspect or debug_get_source_context to look at that caller.

threadId.description: Thread id from debug_list_threads (default: the paused thread, else the focused one)

tools.name: debug_get_variables
tools.description: List the variables visible in a paused frame, grouped by scope (e.g. Locals, Superglobals), with name, value and type. Values of objects and arrays are summaries: pass a variable's variablesReference to list its children, or use debug_inspect to expand a whole structure. Use filter to narrow long lists.

variablesReference.description: Expand this container instead of listing scopes; returns its children, each with its own variablesReference when expandable

filter.description: Only variables whose name contains this text (case-insensitive)

frameId.description: Stack frame id from debug_get_stack_trace (default: the top frame of the thread)

threadId.description: Thread id from debug_list_threads (default: the paused thread, else the focused one)

tools.name: debug_evaluate
tools.description: Evaluate an expression in a paused frame and return its value and type, in the exact syntax of the language being debugged (e.g. "$post->ID" for PHP, "user.name" for JavaScript, "self.items" for Python). It runs in the program: function calls and assignments execute and can change its state. For a nested object prefer debug_inspect; to read many variables, debug_get_variables.

expression.description: Expression in the debugged language, e.g. "count($items)", "get_option('siteurl')", "req.body"

frameId.description: Stack frame id from debug_get_stack_trace (default: the top frame of the thread)

threadId.description: Thread id from debug_list_threads (default: the paused thread, else the focused one)

tools.name: debug_inspect
tools.description: Evaluate a variable or expression and expand its nested structure (objects, arrays, maps) into JSON, a few levels deep. Best for understanding a complex value in one call; like debug_evaluate, the expression runs in the program.

variable.description: Variable or expression in the debugged language, e.g. "$wp_query", "req.body", "self.config"

maxItems.description: Maximum children per level, up to 200 (default 50)

frameId.description: Stack frame id from debug_get_stack_trace (default: the top frame of the thread)

threadId.description: Thread id from debug_list_threads (default: the paused thread, else the focused one)

tools.name: debug_set_variable
tools.description: Change a variable's value while paused, to test a hypothesis without editing code (e.g. set "$cache" to "null", then step on). Uses the debug adapter's setVariable, or setExpression when that isn't available. Returns the new value; fails with an explanation if the adapter can't change variables.

name.description: Variable name as shown by debug_get_variables, e.g. "$count" (PHP) or "count" (JavaScript)

value.description: New value as an expression in the debugged language, e.g. "0", "'abc'", "null", "[]"

variablesReference.description: Container holding a nested variable, from debug_get_variables (default: the frame's scope that has the name)

frameId.description: Stack frame id from debug_get_stack_trace (default: the top frame of the thread)

threadId.description: Thread id from debug_list_threads (default: the paused thread, else the focused one)

tools.name: debug_watch
tools.description: Keep a list of watch expressions for this window and evaluate them all at once, to follow values while stepping: add expressions once, then call action "list" after each step or continue. The list persists across steps and debug sessions until cleared.

action.description: add or remove expressions, list to evaluate all of them now, clear to remove all

expressions.description: Expressions to add or remove, in the debugged language's syntax

frameId.description: Stack frame id from debug_get_stack_trace (default: the top frame of the thread)

threadId.description: Thread id from debug_list_threads (default: the paused thread, else the focused one)

tools.name: debug_get_source_context
tools.description: Show the source lines around where a thread is paused (or around frameId), with the current line marked. Reads the editor's copy, so unsaved edits are included.

lines.description: Lines before and after the current one (default 5, max 50)

frameId.description: Stack frame id from debug_get_stack_trace (default: the top frame of the thread)

threadId.description: Thread id from debug_list_threads (default: the paused thread, else the focused one)

tools.name: debug_get_output
tools.description: Read program output (stdout, stderr) and debug console messages, including logpoint messages from debug_set_breakpoint logMessage. Entries are numbered: pass the returned nextSince as since to get only newer entries; more is true when entries were left out by limit or size. Long entries are shortened. Some adapters log their own protocol traffic here (e.g. PHP with "log": true), so use match to find what you need.

since.description: Only entries after this sequence number (default 0: all kept entries, the last 1000)

category.description: Only this category: stdout, stderr, console or important

match.description: Only entries containing this text (case-insensitive), e.g. "logpoint"

tools.name: debug_set_exception_breakpoints
tools.description: Pause when exceptions or errors are raised. Call without filters to list what the active debug adapter offers (PHP: Notice, Warning, Error, Deprecated, Exception, *; Node: all, uncaught), then call with the filter ids to enable. An empty list turns them off. Applies to the active session only, resets when a new session starts, and is not shown in the editor's Breakpoints panel.

filters.description: Filter ids from the list call, e.g. ["Exception", "Warning"]; [] to turn off

tools.name: editor_open_file
tools.description: Open a file in the editor and optionally move the cursor to a line, e.g. to show the user where the debugger stopped.

tools.name: editor_get_open_files
tools.description: List the files open in editor tabs, with which one is active and which have unsaved changes.

tools.name: workspace_find_file
tools.description: Find files in the window's workspace folders by glob pattern, skipping node_modules. Returns absolute paths, ready for debug_set_breakpoint or editor_open_file.

pattern.description: Glob relative to the workspace folders, e.g. "**/wp-settings.php", "src/**/*.ts"

tools.name: workspace_get_diagnostics
tools.description: Get errors and warnings reported by the editor's language services (TypeScript, PHP, ESLint, ...), per file with line and message.

file.description: Only this file (absolute path); default: every file with problems

severity.description: "error" for errors only, "warning" for errors and warnings (default: everything)
